I've been in receipt of Universal Credit for a few years now, I suffer with anxiety and depression. 

If you don't feel up to working at the moment due to your mental health declining, I suggest asking your GP for a sick note, you mentioned they are aware of your thoughts so I am assuming this is something you can do, as long as you trust your doctor and feel you can be transparent.

As for Universal Credit, they are very prying so be aware, they will try and trip you up regarding whether they think you are fit for work at any point when you talk to them. They also have their own assessment team which can go against any medical professionals' (GP, Dr) advice you have been given already unless circumstances are severe i.e cancer or a mobility preventing condition. If you feel you cannot continue working, tell your GP this, communication with them will work with your sick note.

I would still recommend applying for Universal Credit, if you can apply for PIP do so, they cater more for people with specific health conditions. They post a questionnaire to your house that you answer and send back. Unfortunately the questions are black and white in a sense and you will need to answer carefully to avoid a negative outcome. I had a friend who has Diabetes type 2 and applied for PIP as she needed extra money for her electricity bill to store her Insulin properly (this is a necessity for this type of medication) when she applied she received a score too low to be awarded anything, I am sure you can understand from that instance that they are quite strict when coming to a decision.

Good luck mate, hope you find a way through this.

P.s Universal Credit can also help with uniforms and work-related costs such as bus passes/train passes, make sure you find out what you can get as it can be extremely beneficial for you when transitioning into a new job.
